title: Free childcare hours and a 75% subsidy
subject: The cost and household impact, 2027-28 to 2029-30, of a two-part childcare reform: 15 free hours a week for every child from 9 months to school age, with no work or income test (England), and a 75% subsidy of childcare costs replacing Tax-Free Childcare, with no work test, cap or £100,000 limit and the Universal Credit childcare element kept at 85% (UK-wide); each leg and both together, static and with a labour supply response.
search_terms: 15 free hours all children from nine months cost
extend free childcare to non-working parents cost

free_hours_from_9_months.description: Leg 1: 15 free hours a week for every child from 9 months to school age, regardless of parental work or income, plus a further 15 hours where parents work and earn under £100,000 (England). Costed from age 1: FRS ages are whole years, so the 9-month floor binds at 1 and the 9-to-12-month cohort is not costed (reforms.py).

subsidy_75_replacing_tfc.description: Leg 2: a 75% subsidy of childcare costs replacing Tax-Free Childcare, with no work test, per-child cap or £100,000 limit; the Universal Credit childcare element kept at 85% (UK-wide).

both_legs.description: Both legs run together, with the new free hours displacing paid care before the 75% subsidy applies.

centax_first_15_hours_under_3s_actual_an.description: CenTax section 4.2.3, primary results: the £100,000 limit removed for the first 15 hours for 9-month- to 2-year-olds of working parents and kept for the second 15 hours, with eligibility tested on actual rather than expected ANI (England).

centax_first_15_hours_under_3s_expected_.description: CenTax section 4.2.3, Appendix B: the £100,000 limit removed for the first 15 hours for 9-month- to 2-year-olds of working parents and kept for the second 15 hours, on today's expected-ANI test (England).

ippr_universal_15_hours_under_twos.description: IPPR (September 2022): a universal offer of 15 funded hours a week for every child under two, modelled from six months, added to the 2022 system (England).

ippr_universal_15_hours_two_year_olds.description: IPPR (September 2022): the 15-hour offer for disadvantaged two-year-olds made universal, added to the 2022 system (England).

ippr_reformed_subsidy_75_95.description: IPPR (September 2022): Tax-Free Childcare and the UC childcare element replaced by one subsidy paying 75% of costs for families not on means-tested benefits and 95% for families on them, in a world with 30 free hours for every child from six months to four (England).

nef_universal_family_childcare_promise.description: NEF with Pregnant Then Screwed and JRF (July 2025): the funded hours, Tax-Free Childcare and UC childcare support replaced by 15 free hours for every child from 9 months to 4 plus a cap, at 5% (or 7.5%) of family earnings, on the cost of further hours for working families (England).
